title: Rigveda 7.89: To Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.89: To Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.89 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 548r-548v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.89.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 548r
translation.original_text:
1mo ṣu va̍ruṇa mṛ̱nmaya̍ṁ gṛ̱haṁ rā̍jann a̱haṁ ga̍mam | mṛ̱ḻā su̍kṣatra mṛ̱ḻaya̍ ||
2yad emi̍ prasphu̱rann i̍va̱ dṛti̱r na dhmā̱to a̍drivaḥ | mṛ̱ḻā su̍kṣatra mṛ̱ḻaya̍ ||
3kratva̍ḥ samaha dī̱natā̍ pratī̱paṁ ja̍gamā śuce | mṛ̱ḻā su̍kṣatra mṛ̱ḻaya̍ ||
4a̱pām madhye̍ tasthi̱vāṁsa̱ṁ tṛṣṇā̍vidaj jari̱tāra̍m | mṛ̱ḻā su̍kṣatra mṛ̱ḻaya̍ ||
translation.text:
1LET me not yet, King Varuṇa, enter into the house of clay: Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
2When, Thunderer! I move along tremulous like a wind-blown skin, Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
3O Bright and Powerful God, through want of strength I erred and went astray Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
4Thirst found thy worshipper though he stood in the midst of water-fijods: Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 548r (numbered 69r by the scribe) (OPenn image 548, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.88.4 ‹stotāram vipraḥ sudina-tve ahvām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 548v (numbered 69v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.89.5 ‹-dharma yuyopima mā naḥ›. Verses 7.89.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1mo iti | su | varuṇa | mṛt-mayam | gṛham | rājan | aham | gamam | mṛḷa | su-kṣatra | mṛḷaya
2yat | emi | prasphuran-iva | dṛtiḥ | na | dhmātaḥ | adri-vaḥ | mṛḷa | su-kṣatra | mṛḷaya
3kratvaḥ | samaha | dīnatā | prati-īpam | jagama | śuce | mṛḷa | su-kṣatra | mṛḷaya
4apām | madhye | tasthi-vāṃsam | tṛṣṇā | avidat | jaritāram | mṛḷa | su-kṣatra | mṛḷaya

translation.original_ref: RV 7.89.5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 548v
translation.original_text: <sup>5</sup>yat kiṁ ce̱daṁ va̍ruṇa̱ daivye̱ jane̍ 'bhidro̱ham ma̍nu̱ṣyā̱3̱̍ś carā̍masi | aci̍ttī̱ yat tava̱ dharmā̍ yuyopi̱ma mā na̱s tasmā̱d ena̍so deva rīriṣaḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>5</sup>O Varuṇa, whatever the offence may be which we as men commit against the heavenly host, When through our want of thought we violate thy laws, punish us not, O God, for that iniquity.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 548v (numbered 69v by the scribe) (OPenn image 549, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.89.5 ‹-dharma yuyopima mā naḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 549r (numbered 70r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.90.5 ‹-sacante›. Verse 7.89.5 ends on this page; 7.89.5 begins on fol. 548r (numbered 69r by the scribe).
